Prop Firm vs Broker: Key Differences

A broker lets you trade your own money with leverage. A prop firm lets you trade the firm capital after an evaluation, in exchange for a profit split. The two models suit different traders.

Capital and risk

With a broker you risk your deposit. With a prop firm you risk the evaluation fee, and the firm carries the capital risk on the funded account.

Fees and payouts

Brokers charge spreads and commissions. Prop firms charge evaluation fees and share profits through a profit split. Payout schedules differ widely between prop firms.

Which should you choose?

Traders with small accounts and a proven strategy often prefer a prop firm. Traders who want full control and no rules usually prefer a broker.
